questions.title: Data Bundles, Medical Aid Contributions and Economic Indicators

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 1 shows comparative prices for data bundles of three selected service providers (Telkom, MTN, Smartmobile). Identify the service provider that is the cheapest for both the 500 MB and 1 GB data bundles.
subQuestions.memoText:
Smartmobile
[Award 2 marks for correct service provider]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the total cost of a 500 MB data bundle purchased from MTN at THREE different times during a single month. (MTN 500 MB = R75)
subQuestions.memoText:
Total = $R75 + R75 + R75 = R225$
OR
Total = $R75 \times 3 = R225$

Mark 1: Correct value (R75) read from table
Mark 2: Adding values / multiplying by 3
Mark 3: Simplification (R225)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the cost per megabyte (MB) if you purchase 1 GB from Telkom (R100). Note: 1 GB = 1 000 MB.
subQuestions.memoText:
1 000 MB = 1 GB
Cost per MB = $\frac{R100,00}{1\,000} = R0,10$ / 10c

Mark 1: Dividing by 1 000
Mark 2: Simplification (R0,10 or 10c)

subQuestions.questionText: The probability of randomly selecting a service provider selling a 100 MB data bundle for R20 is $\frac{2}{3}$. Convert this probability to a decimal number, correctly rounded off to TWO decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
Probability = $\frac{2}{3}$ = 0,6666666667 = 0,67

Mark 1: Correct decimal
Mark 2: Correct rounding to 2 decimal places (0,67)

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 2 shows monthly contribution per monthly salary bracket for two different GEMS options (Beryl and Ruby). Identify the option where a person earning a monthly salary of R30 000 pays the same amount for both main member and adult dependant.
subQuestions.memoText:
Beryl
[Award 2 marks for correct option - in the 25 257+ bracket on the Beryl option, both main member (A) and adult dependant (B) pay R2 187]

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the monthly salary bracket of a person who pays R3 540 as the main member.
subQuestions.memoText:
Salary bracket = 15 822 – 27 324
[Award 2 marks for correct bracket - this is the Ruby option, Category A]

subQuestions.questionText: A person earns a gross monthly salary of R14 000. He is the main member of the medical aid and uses the Beryl option. He has one adult dependant and two child dependants. Calculate his total monthly contribution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Beryl option, salary bracket 10 507–14 743:
Main member (A) = R1 669
Adult dependant (B) = R1 656
Child dependant (C) = R952 each

Total contribution = $R1\,669 + R1\,656 + 2(R952)$
= R5 229

Mark 1: All 3 correct values read from table
Mark 2: Adding values
Mark 3: Simplification (R5 229)

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the difference in contributions between the Beryl and Ruby options for a main member with a monthly salary of R15 800.
subQuestions.memoText:
For salary R15 800 (bracket 14 744–25 256 on Beryl; bracket 0–15 821 on Ruby):
Ruby main member = R3 180
Beryl main member = R1 821

Difference = $R3\,180 - R1\,821 = R1\,359$

Mark 1: R3 180 read correctly
Mark 2: R1 821 read correctly
Mark 3: Simplification (R1 359)

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 3 shows the actual and projected percentage changes for certain economic indicators in South Africa from 2023 to 2026. Define the term inflation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Inflation is the increase in the price of goods and services over a given period of time.
OR
Decrease in the purchasing power of a currency over a given period of time.

[Award 2 marks for correct definition]

subQuestions.questionText: State whether the percentages given in the table are discrete or continuous data values.
subQuestions.memoText:
Continuous data
[Award 2 marks for correct classification]

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the projected percentage change for exports during 2025.
subQuestions.memoText:
2,5
Accept: 2,5%
[Award 2 marks for correct value read from table]

subQuestions.questionText: Arrange, in descending order, the projected percentage changes for 2026.
subQuestions.memoText:
4,6   3,6   3,2   2,6   1,8   1,7   –3,0

Mark 1: Correct values
Mark 2: Correct descending order

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the TWO years in which the projected percentage changes for imports remained the same.
subQuestions.memoText:
2025 and 2026
(Both showing 2,6% projected change for imports)

Mark 1: 2025
Mark 2: 2026

questions.title: Tax Certificate, Income Tax and Water Tariffs

subQuestions.questionText: ANNEXURE A shows the tax certificate Frieda Khan received for the tax year ending February 2024. Write down the name of the employer. (Refer to ANNEXURE A in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Cols-Medical Supplies
Accept: Cols
[Award 2 marks for correct name]

subQuestions.label: 2.1.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. If the statement is FALSE, give a suitable reason why: Frieda's bank account is a cheque account.

True

subQuestions.label: 2.1.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. If the statement is FALSE, give a suitable reason why: Frieda does not contribute towards any of the following: pension fund, provident fund or a retirement annuity fund.
subQuestions.memoText:
False – Provident fund contribution code 4003
OR
False – There is a deduction of R36 005,00

Mark 2: Correct reason

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the missing value: A, the total tax, SDL and UIF.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total = $R254\,805,24 + R4\,250,88 + R5\,702,69$
= R264 758,81

Mark 2: Simplification (Answer Only acceptable)

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the missing value: B, the amount for code 3808.
subQuestions.memoText:
Employee's debt = $R895\,108 - (R564\,467 + R38\,093 + R87\,369 + R154\,839 + R36\,005)$
= $R895\,108 - R880\,773$
= R14 335

Mark 2: Subtracting from total

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Frieda's monthly contribution to the UIF.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total UIF = R4 250,88
Ms Khan's contribution = $\frac{R4\,250,88}{2} = R2\,125,44$
Monthly contribution = $\frac{R2\,125,44}{12} = R177,12$

OR

Total UIF = R4 250,88
Monthly contributions = $\frac{R4\,250,88}{12} = R354,24$
Ms Khan's contribution = $\frac{R354,24}{2} = R177,12$

Mark 2: Dividing by 2
Mark 3: Simplification
Mark 4: Dividing by 12

subQuestions.questionText: Determine Frieda's net annual taxable income. You may use the following formula: Net annual taxable income = annual gross salary − (total provident fund contributions) − (20% of travel allowance).
subQuestions.memoText:
Taxable income = $R895\,108 - (R36\,005 \times 2) - (20\% \times R154\,839)$
= $R895\,108 - R72\,010 - R30\,967,80$
= R792 130,20

OR

Non-taxable travel allowance = $20\% \times R154\,839 = R30\,967,80$
Taxable income = $R895\,108 - (R36\,005 \times 2) - R30\,967,80$
= $R895\,108 - R72\,010 - R30\,967,80$
= R792 130,20

Mark 1: Substitution
Mark 2: Calculating 20%
Mark 3: Total provident fund
Mark 4: Travel allowance
Mark 5: Taxable income (R792 130,20)

subQuestions.questionText: ANNEXURE B shows the tax rates for individuals for the tax year ending February 2024. Frieda stated that her employer deducted more than the required amount of PAYE tax from her salary. She felt that she deserved a tax refund from SARS. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether her statement is VALID. (Refer to ANNEXURE B in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Income tax before rebate = $R170\,734 + 39\%(R792\,130,20 - R641\,400)$
= $R170\,734 + 39\%(R150\,730,20)$
= $R170\,734 + R58\,784,78$
= R229 518,778

Income tax after rebate = $R229\,518,778 - R16\,425$
= R213 093,78

Her statement is VALID.
(CA from Question 2.1.5)

Mark 1: Correct bracket
Mark 2: Correct substitution
Mark 3: Tax before rebate
Mark 4: Rebate
Mark 5: Simplification
Mark 6: Conclusion

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 4 indicates the tariffs for domestic water consumption supplied by the eThekwini Municipality for three years for February. Define the term tariff in the given context.
subQuestions.memoText:
The amount charged per kℓ of water used.
[Award 2 marks for explanation]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the amount, including VAT, which Frieda paid for consuming 32 kℓ of water during February 2024. (All tariffs exclude 15% VAT.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Amount excl VAT:
0–6 kℓ: $6 \times R0,00 = R0,00$
>6 kℓ to 25 kℓ: $19 \times R27,80 = R528,20$
>25 kℓ to 30 kℓ: $5 \times R37,90 = R189,50$
>30 kℓ to 45 kℓ: $2 \times R83,60 = R167,20$
Total excl VAT = R884,90

Amount incl VAT = $R884,90 + \frac{R884,90 \times 15}{100}$
= $R884,90 + R132,74$
= R1 017,64

OR (using VAT-included tariffs):
0–6 kℓ: $6 \times R0,00 = R0,00$
>6 kℓ to 25 kℓ: $19 \times R31,97 = R607,43$
>25 kℓ to 30 kℓ: $5 \times R43,585 = R217,93$
>30 kℓ to 45 kℓ: $2 \times R96,14 = R192,28$
Total incl VAT = R1 017,64

Mark 1: Row 1 (0–6 kℓ)
Mark 2: Row 2 (>6 to 25 kℓ)
Mark 3: Row 3 (>25 to 30 kℓ)
Mark 4: Row 4 (>30 to 45 kℓ)
Mark 5: Calculating VAT
Mark 6: Total incl VAT (R1 017,64)

questions.title: School Infrastructure, Electricity Sources and Energy Generation

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 5 shows data indicating schools' access to electricity and the source of electricity across all nine provinces. Write down the province that has the second highest number of schools that use solar power.
subQuestions.memoText:
KwaZulu-Natal (KZN)
[Award 2 marks for correct province]

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in simplified form, the ratio of schools using generators in the Eastern Cape to the schools using generators in the Northern Cape.
subQuestions.memoText:
Eastern Cape generators : Northern Cape generators
= 231 : 11
= 21 : 1

Mark 1: Correct values
Mark 2: Correct order
Mark 3: Simplification (21 : 1)

subQuestions.questionText: The mean number of schools connected to the grid is 2 333,333333. Calculate the missing value, A, the number of schools connected to the grid in Mpumalanga.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total of all values = Mean × 9 = $2\,333,3 \times 9 = 21\,000$

Value of A = $21\,000 - (4\,441 + 945 + 2\,064 + 5\,068 + 3\,470 + 525 + 1\,421 + 1\,452)$
= $21\,000 - 19\,386$
= 1 614

OR

Mean = $\frac{4\,441+945+2\,064+5\,068+3\,470+A+525+1\,421+1\,452}{9}$
$2\,333,3 \times 9 = 19\,386 + A$
$A = 21\,000 - 19\,386 = 1\,614$

Mark 1: Reverse mean calculation / concept of mean
Mark 2: Finding total value / correct substitution
Mark 3: Concept of mean / multiplying by 9
Mark 4: 19 386
Mark 5: Simplification (1 614)

subQuestions.questionText: Daniel stated that Gauteng represented the province with the median number of schools using solar power. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is CORRECT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Arrange values in ascending order:
1; 2; 2; 5; 6; 12; 227; 440; 590

Median = 6
Gauteng = 6

His statement is CORRECT.

OR (with provinces):
1   2   2   5   6   12   227   440   590
MP NW WC FS GP NC LP KZN EC

Mark 1: Arranging values
Mark 2: Identifying the median
Mark 3: Correct province
Mark 4: Conclusion

subQuestions.questionText: The pie chart in ANNEXURE C shows various public schools' access to electricity in the provinces of South Africa. Determine, as a percentage, the probability that a school selected randomly in South Africa is in KwaZulu-Natal. (Refer to ANNEXURE C in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
KwaZulu-Natal = $100\% - (22,33\% + 16,15\% + 9,14\% + 7,30\% + 6,43\% + 13\%)$
= $100\% - 74,35\%$
= 25,65%

Mark 1: Correct values
Mark 2: Adding and subtracting
Mark 3: Simplification (25,65%) [Answer Only acceptable]

subQuestions.questionText: The total number of schools in South Africa that have access to electricity is 22 597. Use the percentage of schools in North West to calculate how many schools have access to electricity.
subQuestions.memoText:
North West percentage = $13\% - 4,18\% - 2,41\% = 6,41\%$

Number of schools = $\frac{6,41 \times 22\,597}{100}$
= 1 448,4677
= 1 448

Mark 1: Correct percentage
Mark 2: Percentage calculation
Mark 3: Simplification
Mark 4: Correct rounding (Accept: 1 449)

subQuestions.questionText: The graphs in ANNEXURE D show the energy generation capacity of the different sources, namely wind power, solar power, hydropower and other power sources generated for Brazil and South Africa during the period 2015 to 2022. Calculate the total terawatt-hours (TWh) generated by Brazil in 2019. (Refer to ANNEXURE D in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Total TWh = $397,88 + 55,43 + 50,34 + 6,59$
= 510,24

Mark 1: Correct values
Mark 2: Adding values
Mark 3: Simplification (510,24)

subQuestions.questionText: A data analyst compared the percentage change in South Africa's wind generation capacity to that of Brazil's percentage change in wind generation capacity for the period 2015 to 2021 and made the following statement: South Africa generated more than 237% wind power compared to that of Brazil during the same period. Show, by means of calculations, whether his statement is VALID. You may use the following formula: Percentage change = ((TWh(2021) − TWh(2015))/TWh(2015)) × 100%.
subQuestions.memoText:
South Africa: % change = $\frac{8,36 - 2,5}{2,5} \times 100\% = 234,4\%$

Brazil: % change = $\frac{362,82 - 373,44}{373,44} \times 100\% = -2,84383033419\%$

Difference = $234,4\% - (-2,84383033419\%)$
= $234,4\% + 2,84383033419\%$
= 237,24384804%

His statement is VALID.

Mark 1: Correct values (SA)
Mark 2: Correct denominator
Mark 3: Simplification (SA)
Mark 4: Correct values (Brazil)
Mark 5: Simplification (Brazil)
Mark 6: Subtracting values
Mark 7: Conclusion

subQuestions.questionText: Explain, using the graphs in ANNEXURE D, why one would state that South Africa generated more solar energy than Brazil during 2022.
subQuestions.memoText:
Different scale used.
OR
The intervals used for South Africa are much smaller.
OR
If one only looks at the graphs without looking at the scale of the vertical axes, you can easily make that mistake. South Africa only generated slightly more than 6 TWh, while Brazil generated above the 50 TWh line.

[Award 2 marks for conclusion]

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 7A shows the number of voters recorded on the voters' roll on 19 March 2024, per age group and gender. Write down the age group which represents the maximum number of voters for both males and females.

30–39
[Award 2 marks for identifying mode/maximum age group]

subQuestions.questionText: Determine, as a percentage, the probability of randomly selecting a male voter from the total number of voters.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total number = $12\,409\,891 + 15\,313\,929 = 27\,723\,820$

Probability = $\frac{12\,409\,891}{27\,723\,820} \times 100\%$
= 44,76%

Mark 1: Correct total
Mark 2: Correct numerator (12 409 891)
Mark 3: Concept of probability

subQuestions.questionText: The range for the number of voters per province is 5 885 202. Calculate the missing value, L, if the Northern Cape had the lowest number of recorded voters.
subQuestions.memoText:
Range = Highest number of voters – Lowest number of voters
$5\,885\,202 = 6\,542\,033 - L$
$L = 6\,542\,033 - 5\,885\,202$
L = 656 831

OR

Total number of voters = $12\,409\,891 + 15\,313\,929 = 27\,723\,820$
L = $27\,723\,820 - (3\,439\,325 + 1\,456\,935 + 6\,542\,033 + 5\,738\,272 + 2\,779\,668 + 2\,025\,074 + 1\,768\,580 + 3\,317\,102)$
= $27\,723\,820 - 27\,066\,989$
= 656 831

Mark 1: Correct concept / total voters
Mark 2: Correct substitution
Mark 3: Changing subject of formula / adding and subtracting
Mark 4: Simplification (656 831) [Answer Only acceptable]

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the trend in the number of recorded female voters with regard to the different age groups.
subQuestions.memoText:
From 20–39 years the number of registered female voters increases.
From 40 years and above the number of registered female voters decreases.

Mark 2: Age increase, voters decrease

questions.title: Soccer Statistics, Salary Conversion, Compound Interest and AFCON Prize Money

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 8 shows the top ten goal scorers, the number of games played and the number of goals scored by the national team. Identify the player who scored an average of exactly one goal for every three matches played.
subQuestions.memoText:
Player I (54 games played, 18 goals scored: $\frac{54}{18} = 3$, ratio 3:1, i.e. one goal for every three matches)
[Award 2 marks for correct player]

subQuestions.questionText: Neo compared player G with player C and made the following claim: Player G had a better games-played to goals-scored ratio compared to player C. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his claim is VALID.
subQuestions.memoText:
Player G: 30 : 21 = 1 : 0,7
Player C: 50 : 28 = 1 : 0,56

His statement is VALID.

Mark 1: Both correct values (Player G)
Mark 2: Simplification (Player G)
Mark 3: Both correct values (Player C)
Mark 4: Like simplification (Player C)
Mark 5: Verification / conclusion

subQuestions.questionText: Neo earns an annual salary of €18 000. The official currency in the Ivory Coast is the franc of the West African communities (XOF). On 16 March 2024, the exchange rate was €1 = 656 XOF. Calculate Neo's monthly salary in XOF.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual salary = $€18\,000 = 18\,000 \times 656$ XOF $= 11\,808\,000$ XOF
Monthly salary = $\frac{11\,808\,000 \text{ XOF}}{12} = 984\,000$ XOF

OR

Monthly salary in euro = $\frac{18\,000}{12} = €1\,500$
Monthly salary in XOF = $1\,500 \times 656 = 984\,000$ XOF

Mark 1: Converting to XOF
Mark 2: Simplification
Mark 3: Dividing by 12
Mark 4: Simplification (984 000 XOF)

subQuestions.questionText: Neo invested €2 500 for 30 months at a compound interest rate of 12,6% per annum, compounded annually. Calculate, in euros, the amount he will receive at the end of the investment period.
subQuestions.memoText:
Amount end of year 1 = $€2\,500 \times \frac{112,6}{100} = €2\,815$

Amount end of year 2 = $€2\,815 \times \frac{112,6}{100} = €3\,169,69$

Interest for half of year 3 (6 months out of 12) = $€3\,169,69 \times \frac{12,6}{100} \times \frac{6}{12} = €199,69$

Total amount = $€3\,169,69 + €199,69 = €3\,369,38$

Mark 1: Calculating interest (year 1)
Mark 2: Simplification / interest year 2
Mark 3: Amount for year 2
Mark 4: Calculating months (half of year 3)
Mark 5: Simplification (€3 369,38)

subQuestions.questionText: TABLE 9 shows the prize money the teams receive for reaching different stages in the AFCON tournament. Write down the total number of teams that will play in the quarter-finals.
subQuestions.memoText:
8
[Award 2 marks for correct value - 8 teams play in the quarter-finals (16-team round of 16 produces 8 quarter-finalists)]

subQuestions.questionText: The prize money for the 2024 AFCON Tournament was 40% more than the prize money for the previous tournament. Determine, to the nearest $, the total prize money for the previous AFCON Tournament.
subQuestions.memoText:
Previous + 40% = 2024
2024 = 140%
Previous = $32\,000\,000 \times \frac{100}{140}$
= $\$22\,857\,142,86$
= \$22 857 143

OR: $32\,000\,000 \div 1,4 = \$22\,857\,143$

Mark 1: Calculating 140%
Mark 2: Percentage calculation
Mark 3: Simplification
Mark 4: Rounding (\$22 857 143)

subQuestions.questionText: Verify, showing ALL calculations, that the total prize money awarded to the 24 countries was $32 000 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
Total prize money:
Winner (1st): \$7 000 000
Runner-up (2nd): \$4 000 000
Losing semi-finalists (3rd & 4th): $2 \times \$2\,500\,000 = \$5\,000\,000$
Losing quarter-finalists: $4 \times \$1\,300\,000 = \$5\,200\,000$
Losing in round of 16: $8 \times \$800\,000 = \$6\,400\,000$
Two best 3rd-placed teams in groups: $2 \times \$700\,000 = \$1\,400\,000$
Six lowest in groups: $6 \times \$500\,000 = \$3\,000\,000$

GRAND TOTAL = \$32 000 000

Mark 1: Winner + Runner-up
Mark 2: 2 × Semi-finalist
Mark 3: 4 × Quarter-finalists
Mark 4: 8 × Round of 16
Mark 5: 2 × Best 3rds in groups
Mark 6: 6 × Stage low ranked
